description: SKY130 130 nm ROM view, v2.  Supersedes abi3-cost-sky130-rom-v1, whose 100 MHz clock was an assumption; a routed engine of this machine closes at 38.8 MHz on the same open foundry PDK.  The ROM read latency is still an ngspice measurement of a three-bitline slice, not a macro.  Generated by tools/build_abi3_cost_tables.py from the artifacts each characterized parameter cites; run that tool with --check to verify this file still matches them.

clock.frequency_hz.note: minimum post-route fmax over the routed blocks that implement a modelled engine family: vector_add_unit (vector) 1.48596e+08 Hz, reduction_s8_g2 (reduction) 1.7137e+08 Hz.  add_bf16_sram_engine closes at 3.88071e+07 Hz and is excluded: SUPERSEDED as the vector engine by ot_vector_add_unit, on this view as well as on asap7.  One element per cycle through a combinational BF16 adder, 38.8 MHz.  Reported because it was routed; excluded because the machine no longer instantiates it.  The excluded blocks marked SUPERSEDED were the previous implementations of engine families that have since been redesigned; this view's clock moved because the design changed, not because the same design was re-measured.  No block has been routed for engine dma, tensor, attention, route, selection, state, link, so this clock is an upper bound on the machine's core clock and can only fall as those engines are routed.

engine.reduction.work_per_lane_cycle.note: one ot_reduction_endpoint instance accepted 4096 reduction.elements in 4103 clocks, measured identically on iverilog, verilator.  4096 flits accepted in 4103 clocks with the downstream always ready; the trailing clocks are the last group draining, so the steady-state rate is the limit this figure approaches from below.  This block has a full place-and-route result in both physical views (results/physical_abi3/sky130hd/reduction_s8_g2/pnr.json, results/physical_abi3/asap7/reduction_s8_g2/pnr.json) from the same source file the bench compiled, so its rate and its frequency are the same design and not two.  The hand-written table assumed 1.0 here; the measurement says the assumption was very nearly right, which is a result and not a correction.

engine.tensor.work_per_lane_cycle.note: one ot_ta_matmul_bf16_sram_engine instance retired 33554432 work units (tensor.multiplications + tensor.additions) in 97012165 cycles under q_proj_iverilog; the independent q_proj_verilator run of the same campaign took 97010897 cycles, a 0.00% spread on the rate.  Replicated on a second operator: results/tensor_accelerator/qwen3_rtl_kv_proj_campaign.json retires 16777216 work units in 48506095 cycles, 0.345878513 work/lane/cycle.  The campaign's memories are behavioural, so this rate is the RTL's own cycle behaviour under that memory model and not a post-layout timing result; it is a rate, so it is independent of the clock.

engine.vector.work_per_lane_cycle.note: one ot_ta_head_rmsnorm_bf16_sram_engine instance retired 5120 work units (vector.elements) in 63589 cycles under head_rmsnorm_iverilog; the independent head_rmsnorm_verilator run of the same campaign took 69900 cycles, a 9.03% spread on the rate.  This is not one rate for the whole family: a different vector-family engine, ot_ta_rope_bf16_sram_engine, measures 0.135783807 work/lane/cycle in results/tensor_accelerator/qwen3_rtl_rope_campaign.json (5120 work units in 37707 cycles), 1.69x this one.  The table carries the slower of the measured operators, because a family rate that is faster than an operator the family has to run is a rate no run supports.  The campaign's memories are behavioural, so this rate is the RTL's own cycle behaviour under that memory model and not a post-layout timing result; it is a rate, so it is independent of the clock.

hbm.bytes_per_cycle_per_channel.note: one HBM2e stack, divided across hbm.channels.default and this table's clock
hbm.bytes_per_cycle_per_channel.source: configs/hardware/technology_inputs.json#packaging_inputs.hbm2e_stack.bandwidth_bytes_s (derived from source_facts.a100_sxm_80gb, evidence "published:NVIDIA A100 product page and NVIDIA Ampere architecture whitepaper")

hbm.channels.default.note: ADR-003 section 19 defers HBM channel and stack count; 8 channels per HBM2e stack is the modelling choice, not a measurement

hbm.interleave_bytes.note: channel interleave granularity; no floorplan fixes it

hbm.read_latency_cycles.note: no HBM latency figure exists anywhere in this repository; this is a modelling choice and every HBM-bound result inherits it

hbm.transaction_bytes.note: the DMA RTL issues 64-byte HBM bursts; correlation.hbm_burst_bytes=64 with 8192 bytes over 128 requests

host.bytes_per_cycle.note: host-visible window bandwidth over the management path

model.max_modeled_transactions_per_acces.note: above this, one access reserves per-unit time in bulk: total occupancy stays exact, only the interleave with other traffic is coarsened

rom.arrays.default.note: ADR-003 section 19 defers ROM macro geometry

rom.bytes_per_cycle_per_array.note: no ROM macro bandwidth exists in this repository; the SPICE evidence is a 3-bitline slice, not a macro

rom.read_latency_cycles.note: worst-PVT bitline discharge delay of the SKY130 NOR-ROM read slice (ss, 1.62 V, 125 C, 1024 rows, 5 fF), ngspice 36 on SKY130 PDK v0.20.1, 51/51 cases passing. It is a three-bitline circuit proxy with synthetic lumped bitline capacitance, not a ROM macro; the extracted variant measures 0.06088713 ns

sequencer.fetch_cycles.note: one 32-byte instruction fetched per cycle from the program buffer

sequencer.issue_cycles.note: one descriptor issued per cycle; the ABI 3.0 microsequencer is in-order

sequencer.predicate_cycles.note: ADR-003 5.2 predicate evaluation, including a predicated-off instruction

sequencer.wait_check_cycles.note: scoreboard lookup for one WAIT_ACQUIRE set

sram.bytes_per_cycle_per_port.note: configs/hardware/tensor_accelerator_development_v7.json#sram (declared capability shape; evidence.classification="uncharacterized_development") declares word_bytes=16; there is no qualified SRAM macro in this repository (claim_boundary.qualified_sram_macro=false)

sram.interleave_bytes.note: fine-grained bank interleave. The declared development capability instead uses bank_address_stride=1048576, which would place a small working set entirely in one bank; the parameter is exposed so that choice can be swept rather than assumed away

sram.ports_per_bank.default.note: configs/hardware/tensor_accelerator_development_v7.json#sram (declared capability shape; evidence.classification="uncharacterized_development") declares read_ports_per_bank=1 and write_ports_per_bank=1

sram.read_latency_cycles.note: no SRAM macro access time exists in this repository

state.backing_storage_class.note: STATE objects are timed as if they lived in this storage class; ADR-003 does not bind the placement of a state resource
